trust_decision.summary: Whether a state-changing custom back-end action reached through the Backend dispatcher (?do=<module>&key=<action>) may run without a valid Contao request token (rt); the fix adds the decision per action, once in the legacy DCA callback tl_opt_in::resendToken and once in the manager-bundle DebugController, and emits rt into the debug menu link.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary ('cross-site request forgery in custom backend actions') plus the first changed source hunk point at the opt-in resend callback: a ?do=opt_in&key=resend custom action that sends an e-mail and had no request-token check, reached from the routine DCA operation link at tl_opt_in.php:63-72.

fix_sites.module_kind: core-bundle legacy DCA / BE_MOD custom action
core-bundle DCA operation definition / UI producer

fix_sites.entry_point: every back-end page render (MenuEvent header menu builds the do=debug link)
fix_sites.module_kind: manager-bundle event listener / token producer in the UI

fix_sites.entry_point: service construction of DebugController (csrfTokenManager + csrfTokenName arguments)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The newsletter 'block' action is a data-container operation whose link is built by Backend::addToUrl and therefore already carries an rt parameter, so it looks like the generic data-container request-token check covers it; and the advisory/fix only names the opt-in resend and the debug toggle.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The resend button must stay clickable: the fix renders the operation as a POST form (method=POST) whose href no longer carries rt and whose body carries REQUEST_TOKEN, so the callback's own check is deliberately skipped on non-safe methods; an unconditional isTokenValid(Input::get('rt')) check, or a POST form without the hidden token field, breaks every legitimate click.

O6_input_shapes: request token as a GET query parameter 'rt' (Input::get('rt') in the DCA callback; $request->query->get('rt') in the manager controller)
request token as a POST body field 'REQUEST_TOKEN', including inside a root-level array, validated by the global RequestTokenListener
the same operation rendered either as a plain GET link (rt in the URL) or as a POST form via 'method' => 'POST' (rt removed from the URL, token moved into the body)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: contao_backend?do=newsletter&key=block&id=N - deletes the newsletter recipient and writes a deny-list entry on a GET request with no token validation
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The operation link already includes rt because Backend::addToUrl appends it for methodless operations, so it appears covered by the generic DC_Table token check; it is also in the newsletter bundle, outside the module named by the advisory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different bundle/package (newsletter-bundle) and different module (content/newsletter); reached through newsletter-bundle/contao/config/config.php:27

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second key action on the opt_in module (e.g. 'invalidate' => array('tl_opt_in', 'invalidateToken')) next to 'resend'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Custom module actions are registered exactly this way, and the opt-in table already has a state-changing row operation, so a maintainer would naturally add another one here without touching the DCA constructor's allowlist.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A sibling row operation (e.g. 'invalidate' with a button_callback) that mutates tl_opt_in on a GET link
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The resend operation is defined in this operations array with a button_callback and no method, so copying it for a second lifecycle action would reproduce the same missing-token sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third action on the manager-bundle BE_MOD debug module (e.g. key=reset) calling another updateJwtCookie-style method
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The manager-bundle registers enable/disable as BE_MOD key actions in manager-bundle/contao/config/config.php:14-20; adding one more admin action there is a one-line change.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate Input::get('rt') only inside tl_opt_in::resendToken (or only switch that one operation to POST), assuming the global POST token check then covers every custom back-end action.

O7 is recorded as 'none': the rt producer (Backend::addToUrl / ContaoCsrfTokenManager::getDefaultTokenValue) and the check (isTokenValid) share the same session-backed token storage, so no schema/serializer/cache/config-loader boundary applies.
